note.text: Screening estimate from a photo-based sample using IBMWP family scores (Alba-Tercedor et al. (2002), family scores as in MAGRAMA (2011)), banded on IASPT; not a Water Framework Directive classification. A formal classification needs a standardised kick sample, laboratory identification and comparison against a reference site.
Sensitive animals are thinning out. Something is putting the stream under pressure.
A vision model, shown the sample photograph without the observer's identifications, independently agreed on 1 of them; the observer kept their own identification on 1 after comparing.

Limitations: 4 habitat question(s) went unanswered (foam_or_sheen, litter, sediment_deposit, shade), so the pressure score covers less of the site; 8 of 12 habitat questions were answered; each unanswered one leaves part of the site undescribed

text.div: Urban stream ecological status, citizen screening: Moderate

note.text: 1 sensitive family from the mayfly/stonefly/caddisfly groups (Plecoptera) were found. These animals do not persist in polluted water.
Tolerant animals outnumber sensitive ones (2 to 1). That usually means the stream is under constant pressure rather than recovering from a one-off spill.
Average sensitivity of the families present (IASPT) is 4.7 out of 10.

The IBMWP total is 14. On IBMWP's own scale that is class 'Bad', but that scale assumes a standardised sample across every habitat in the reach; one tray finds far fewer families, so the total reads low. The band above is read from the IASPT instead.

coding.display: One Health rule: human health, rain ahead

code.text: Heavy rain is forecast, so plan water contact around it

component.valueString: 22 mm of rain is forecast here in the next 48 hours (Open-Meteo)

note.text: Possible harmful algal bloom, so avoid contact with the water: Keep out of the water and keep children and dogs out, including from spray. Do not let animals drink it. Report the bloom to your local environmental agency. Only a laboratory can tell whether it is toxin-producing cyanobacteria. Confirm the observation in the app to raise this to a full alert.

Conditions suit mosquito breeding: Remove containers and litter that hold water near the bank, and tell the municipality about standing water that does not drain. Getting the water flowing again fixes this for good. Insecticide doesn't, and it kills the stream's own insects along with the mosquitoes.

Heavy rain is forecast, so plan water contact around it: Put off paddling, dog swims and river-day kick samples until two dry days after the rain. If you can, come back within a day of it: a before-and-after pair at the same spot is the clearest evidence of whether an overflow feeds this stream.

text.div: One Health signal: human health: concern

component.valueString: a surface algal bloom, which can produce toxins that kill dogs within hours of drinking or swimming

note.text: Do not let animals drink here or swim: Keep dogs on a lead past this stretch and carry water for them. Warn other owners; a sign at the access point works.
